title: Detecting high-dimensional entanglement with simple measurements
authors: Suraj Goel, Alexander Bernal, Gabriele Cobucci, Will McCutcheon, Mehul Malik, Armin Tavakoli
abstract: The standard benchmark for high-dimensional entanglement is the number of dimensions in which entanglement must be present in order to generate the state. This is called the Schmidt number and its detection is usually based on implementing an appropriate set of local basis measurements. However, as quantum technology brings increasingly large physical dimensions within reach, the implementation of such measurements typically becomes more costly. Here, we develop a scheme for detecting Schmidt numbers based only on sequences of single-qubit observables. These measurements are simpler to implement as they require only low-depth quantum circuits. Using up to sixteen-dimensional photonic spatial mode entanglement and multi-plane light conversion technology, we demonstrate how it simplifies setup complexity and successfully detects the maximal (or close-to-maximal) Schmidt number. Our results reveal that simple and more scalable measurements are sufficient to detect high-dimensional entanglement properties.
summary: The paper presents a novel, experimentally simpler method for detecting high-dimensional entanglement (Schmidt number) using only single-qubit measurements on photonic spatial modes. By developing and testing a witness parameter based on Pauli observables, the authors show that complex certification tasks can be achieved with significantly reduced experimental complexity compared to standard methods.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a measurement scheme to detect high-dimensional entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number ($k$), that avoids complex local basis measurements.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that simple measurements using only sequences of single-qubit observables are sufficient and scalable enough to certify high-dimensional entanglement in photonic systems.
method: They introduce a witness parameter $W_n(ho_{AB})$ derived from Pauli string observables, which allows for bounding the Schmidt number based on experimentally feasible low-depth quantum circuits.
model_or_system: The work utilizes high-dimensional photonic spatial mode entanglement, implemented using Multi-Plane Light Converters (MPLCs) and single-photon detectors. The theoretical framework involves analyzing Pauli string operators ($S_{n,j}$) acting on the bipartite state $ho_{AB}$.
key_observables: The witness parameter $W_n(ho_{AB})$, the Schmidt number ($k$), and fidelity ($F$) are key observables.
important_parameters: The local dimension ($d=2^n$) and the entanglement dimension ($k$) are central parameters. The depth of the required quantum circuit is a critical complexity parameter.
main_assumptions: Assumptions include the validity of using Pauli string measurements to bound the Schmidt number, and in some derivations, assuming pure states or restricting analysis to diagonal operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between complex conventional measurement circuits versus the proposed low-depth circuit scheme. Other figures detail the experimental setup involving SPDC sources and MPLC components for measuring coincidence matrices.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical bounds on entanglement measures ($\alpha(n, k)$) using multiple mathematical approaches (fidelity vs. element-wise maximization). It then experimentally validates these concepts by implementing the measurement scheme using photonic systems, culminating in numerical results that confirm the detection capability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses experimental bottlenecks in quantum information processing by proposing resource-efficient entanglement verification protocols applicable to scalable photonic quantum technologies.
